family_history: Mother alive at 84, no cognitive issues

social_history.occupation: Retired chef and restaurant owner; closed restaurant 18 months ago after health department violations and staff complaints
social_history.alcohol: Escalating — husband reports 6 glasses wine daily (previously social only)

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert. Previously creative and organized chef now severely disinhibited. Talks constantly over examiner. MMSE 20/30. FAB 9/18 — severely impaired across all frontal tasks. Category fluency: 6/60 seconds. Bilateral frontal release signs. Severe perseverative behavior observed.
neurological_exam.motor: Mild bilateral upper extremity rigidity. 5/5 strength.
neurological_exam.additional: Hyperorality — took and ate a granola bar from examiner's desk mid-exam.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive disinhibition, compulsive eating, and personality change in a 61-year-old chef over 2 years.
patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. R. is a 61-year-old left-handed woman referred for evaluation of progressive personality changes over 2 years. Her husband describes her as formerly a meticulous, creative chef who ran a well-regarded restaurant for 15 years. Two years ago, she began making erratic decisions at the restaurant — over-ordering food, screaming at staff in front of customers, and serving meals she had taken bites from. She received multiple health code violations before closing the restaurant 18 months ago. At home, she eats continuously, consuming multiple meals in succession, and has gained 20 lbs. She obsessively rearranges pots and pans in the kitchen in the same pattern repeatedly for hours. She makes offensive remarks to neighbors. She has had several minor car accidents due to impulsive driving. Her wine consumption has escalated from social to 6 glasses daily, which she denies. Husband confirms she shows no distress or insight. No family history of dementia. Thyroid function was checked by PCP and is normal.

findings.location: bilateral frontal lobes, orbitofrontal and dorsolateral

volumetrics.frontal_lobes: 25% below norms — most severe case in series

additional_observations: Preserved posterior parietal and occipital cortex
mri.impression: Very severe bilateral frontal and anterior temporal atrophy. Clinical correlation recommended.

advanced_imaging.impression: Very severe bilateral frontotemporal hypometabolism. Diagnostic of bvFTD. Most severe case metabolically in this series.
recommended_actions: Driving assessment — patient has had accidents

output.interpretation: Opening pressure: 125 mmH2O. WBC: 1 cell/mm3 (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 39 mg/dL. Glucose: 58 mg/dL (ratio 0.66). Abeta42: 870 pg/mL (normal). Total tau: 200 pg/mL (normal). Phospho-tau 181: 34 pg/mL (normal). NfL: 2,490 pg/mL (elevated).

recommended_actions: Level of care discussion — may need memory care soon

output.proposed: Sertraline 50 mg and trazodone 50 mg at bedtime for behavioral symptoms
interactions: Hydrochlorothiazide + sertraline: low interaction; monitor electrolytes
warnings: Combination SSRI + trazodone: low serotonin syndrome risk at low doses; monitor
alternatives: Quetiapine 25 mg for severe agitation only if needed and with specialist input

results.title: Driving in FTD
results.finding: bvFTD patients have markedly elevated accident risk due to impulsivity and poor judgment; should not drive even with mild symptoms

output.summary: Patients with bvFTD should not drive — impulsivity and poor judgment create extreme accident risk. Patient has already had accidents. License revocation reporting may be required per state law.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), sporadic — advanced stage

differential.key_features: Amyloid negative, frontal pattern, normal hippocampi
Alcohol escalation is symptom of FTD disinhibition, not cause; imaging pattern diagnostic of FTD

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Very severe bifrontal and anterior temporal atrophy

optimal_actions.action: IMMEDIATE: Revoke driving privileges — accidents have occurred
Discuss level of care — close to memory care threshold

critical_actions: Diagnose bvFTD — very severe presentation with major safety concerns
URGENT: Patient must not drive — accidents already occurred, impulsivity extreme
Level of care planning — advanced stage may need memory care soon
key_reasoning_points: Very severe bvFTD with FAB 9/18 and MMSE 20/30 — advanced stage requiring high level of care and immediate safety interventions
Driving must cease — accidents are documented and impulsivity is extreme
Alcohol escalation is frontal disinhibition symptom, not cause
Normal thyroid function (on treatment) and other labs confirm this is not reversible
